I declared myself a PM because the PM on the project quit, and I just threw myself headfirst in understanding carriers and OEMs and certification, as well as Android and operating systems, and just learned a ton. And I'm happy I brought that project to an end, because it had been going on for a long time. And sometimes, the best thing you can do is execute an idea that doesn't have market fit well, just to decide whether or not the idea was a good idea in the first place. (01:01:33): Another big mistake I made during my Instagram tenure was the first version of Reels was built on top of Stories. Stories had a ton of momentum. This was, I think, 2019, and we were trying to build Reels into Stories because we were trying to build in the thing that was growing the fastest. But it was not a strong foundation. The read-through rate on stories is relatively low. There's way more stories than most people have time to consume. (01:01:59): So most of the Reels were never seen, and then they disappeared. And if we had the version of Reels that we launched in, I think it was the summer of 2020, in the summer of 2019 ... I think TikTok is still big and important, but I don't think it's as big as it is now, because when they really took off was when the pandemic hit, and a bunch of people had a lot of time at home, and we're looking for a little bit of joy, and we're totally fine with our phone having sound on. (01:02:32): And so if you look at the numbers, 2020 is when they exploded, and we were out of position. And on one hand, I'm a designer, I'm trying to not add new things to the product. I'm trying to extend existing primitives, and that was the idea. On the other hand, I was wrong. And it's a pretty big fork on the road if you just look at the overall business over the last eight years.
turns.zh: ——和 HTC 的一台硬件。那是 spectacular 的失败。那一年一年半我学到的比任何一年都多，因为之前我只是设计 manager。PM 离职后我自封 PM，一头扎进理解运营商、OEM、认证，以及 Android 和操作系统，学了一大堆。我很高兴我把那个项目结束了，因为它拖了很久。有时你能做的最好的事就是把一个没有市场契合度的 idea 执行好，以决定它到底是不是好 idea。(01:01:33)：我在 Instagram 任内犯的另一个大错是 Reels 第一版建在 Stories 上。Stories 当时势头很猛，应该是 2019 年，我们想把 Reels 建在增长最快的东西里。但这不是个好基础。Stories 的读完率相对低。Stories 比大多数人能消费的多得多。(01:01:59)：所以大多数 Reels 从未被看到，然后就消失了。如果我们在 2019 年夏天上线的是 2020 年夏天那版 Reels……我觉得 TikTok 仍然重要，但不会像现在这么大，因为它真正起飞是疫情时，很多人在家有很多时间，找点乐子，完全接受手机开声音。(01:02:32)：你看数字，2020 年它爆发，而我们位置不对。一方面我是设计师，不想给产品加新东西，想延伸现有 primitives，这是当时的想法。另一方面我错了。如果你只看……

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You created a lot of economic opportunity in the world, allowing TikTok to grow.
turns.zh: 你给世界创造了很多经济机会，让 TikTok 增长。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Yeah, it's good. I'm glad they exist.
turns.zh: 对，挺好。我很高兴他们存在。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, final question. I'm curious just about your screen time policy with your kids. I know you have three kids. There's a lot of concern these days about Instagram not being great for people, not for kids. A lot of tech executives don't let their kids use devices while they're building the product. As head of Instagram, how do you think about screen time with your kids?
turns.zh: 好，最后一个问题。我好奇你给孩子们的屏幕时间政策。我知道你有三个孩子。现在很多人担心 Instagram 对人、对孩子不好。很多科技高管自己造产品但不让自己孩子用。作为 Instagram 负责人，你怎么想孩子的屏幕时间？

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: The key thing for me is boundaries. It's also about education and having conversations with them. But my kids are too young to use social media. They're 10, 8, and 6. But they each have an iPad. They have to earn their time. So they have different ways they earn their time. It's usually about sitting down to do your homework. Three times for half an hour each gets you a total of 90 minutes on the weekend, and then they can use that time on the weekend. But you kind of have to set that boundary, where it can't just be they ask for it, and you give it to them. I think that matters a lot. And then I'm pretty opinionated about what they do on it. I approve what apps that they have. I think parents should be approving what apps kids specifically are downloading onto their devices. We've been advocating for this at a policy level for a long time at Meta. I think those things help a lot. (01:04:22): There are some exceptions. One is planes. It's just about surviving. I don't know if you've ever ... For those of you who are parents-
turns.zh: 对我来说关键是边界。也关乎教育和和他们对话。但我孩子太小还不能用社交媒体。他们 10、8、6 岁。他们各自有 iPad。他们得赚取时间。有不同赚取方式。通常是坐下来做作业。三次每次半小时，总共换来周末 90 分钟，他们周末可以用。但你得设那个边界，不能他要你就给。我觉得这很重要。然后我对他们用什么比较 opionated。我批准他们有什么 app。我觉得父母该批准孩子往设备上装什么 app。我们在 Meta 政策层面倡导这个很久了。我觉得这些很有帮助。(01:04:22)：有些例外。一是飞机。就是求生。我不知道你有没有……对于各位父母——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm going to be, yeah.
turns.zh: 我快当了，对。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Yeah, that's just like, "All right." It's a 10-hour flight or 8-hour flight. It's like, yeah, you just need to get through it. (01:04:40): The other one that I'm starting to experiment with my 10-year-old with is ... So schools are interesting because I think I'm pretty supportive of a no phone in classrooms that's happening more and more. I think that's just probably good for education. And I do also know, in the world of AI, that there's concern about kids using AI and not learning critical thinking skills, and I think that's a valid concern. But I also am worried about kids not learning how to leverage AI and then being sort of at a disadvantage. So that's a balance. I think you need both. (01:05:14): So with my eldest, we started vibe coding recently together. He just loves video games. So I was like, "All right, let's make a video game." And so he's made this 19-level platformer game that kind of looks like an eight bit version of Super Mario from when I was a kid. But each level has its own theme, its own types of monsters. There's a store where you can buy different skins or weapons. And it's unbelievable what a 10-year-old who still types with three fingers can do with just a couple hours of sitting together. But that is more of a, "I want you to learn how to make things. I want you to be thinking, not just playing games. And I'm going to sit with you, and we're going to do this together." (01:06:03): So to me, these are the things that matter, boundaries, scoping it down to the activities you think are healthy for your kid. Every kid is different. But I do think you want your kids to be digitally literate, AI literate, because I think if they're not, they're going to be at a disadvantage. But you also don't want it to be a free for all.
turns.zh: 对，就是「好吧」。10 小时或 8 小时航班。对，你就是得过。(01:04:40)：另一个我开始和 10 岁的试的……学校这块挺有意思，我比较支持教室里无手机，越来越多这样。我觉得这对教育大概好。我也知道在 AI 时代有人担心孩子用 AI 而不学批判性思维，我觉得这是合理担忧。但我也担心孩子不学用 AI 然后处于劣势。所以是平衡。我觉得两者都要。(01:05:14)：所以和我老大，我们最近一起 vibe coding。他就是爱电子游戏。我说「好，我们做个游戏。」他做了个 19 关的平台游戏，有点像我小时候的 8 位超级马里奥。每关有自己的主题、自己的怪物。还有商店买不同皮肤或武器。一个还用三根手指打字的 10 岁孩子，和我们坐一起几个小时能做到这个，难以置信。但这更多是「我要你学怎么造东西，我要你思考，不只是玩游戏。我坐在你旁边，我们一起做。」(01:06:03)：所以对我来说这些是重要的：边界、限定到你认为对孩子健康的活动。每个孩子不同。但我确实觉得你要让孩子 digitally literate、AI literate，否则他们会处于劣势。但你也不想让它完全放任。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is selfishly useful for me as ... I have a three-year-old, and I'm trying to figure all this stuff out, so this is useful for me to figure out a strategy.
turns.zh: 这对我这个……我有个三岁的，自私地有用，我在琢磨这些事，这帮我理清策略。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: It's a thing. And you're not that far off. You're really just not that far off. It's going to happen in a couple years.
turns.zh: 是这么回事。你也不远了。真的不远了。几年后就会发生。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Vibe coding next year, let's do it.
turns.zh: 明年 vibe coding，来吧。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: I couldn't believe. I tried to do it six months ago and it just totally didn't work. And then now, with newer models, it's been amazing.
turns.zh: 我都不敢相信。我六个月前试过完全不行。现在新模型出来了，太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's their platform of choice? Are they a Claude Code person?
turns.zh: 他们用什么平台？是 Claude Code 的人吗？

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Yeah, my 10-year-old is using Claude Code right now.
turns.zh: 对，我 10 岁的现在用 Claude Code。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay.
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: But we will see. We'll see how that goes.
turns.zh: 但走着瞧。看怎么发展。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Adam, I'm going to let you go. Thank you so much for being here. You're just like such a gem of a person. It's just so obvious how clear-
turns.zh: Adam，放你走。非常感谢你来。你真是个人才。非常明显你有多——

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Thank you. I appreciate that.
turns.zh: 谢谢。我很 appreciate。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... like how authentic you are, and just how deeply you think about everything. So I really appreciate you being here.
turns.zh: ——真实，以及你对一切都思考得多深。所以真的很感谢你来。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Yeah, I appreciate you bringing me on. Been a fan for a long time. It's nice to finally get to have a conversation.
turns.zh: 对，很 appreciate 你请我来。粉丝很久了。终于能聊一次真好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I really appreciate that. I really appreciate that. Let me just ask you this final question I ask everyone, what's a way that listeners can be useful to you?
turns.zh: 非常感谢。非常感谢。让我问你我对每个人问的最后一个问题：听众怎么能帮到你？

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: I just think ... You don't even have to tell this to other people, but just remember that this world and technology is complicated, and there are almost always trade-offs. And you can totally disagree with the decisions I or we make, but just remember that we are people here trying to make these decisions, just trying to do the best we can. And I actually do invite the criticism and the critique and the feedback. But know that none of these contentious debates are nearly as simple as most people pretend to make them out to be.
turns.zh: 我只是觉得……你甚至不用告诉别人，但记住这个世界和技术很复杂，几乎总有取舍。你完全可以不同意我或我们做的决定，但记住我们是人，在做这些决定，尽力做到最好。我其实真心邀请批评和反馈。但要知道这些有争议的辩论没有大多数人假装的那么简单。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wise words. Adam, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 智慧之言。Adam，非常感谢你来。

turns.speaker: Adam Mosseri
turns.en: Pleasure. Thank you, Lenny.
turns.zh: 荣幸。谢谢你，Lenny。

turns.en: Bye, everyone. (01:08:06): Thank you so much for listening. turns.zh: 大家再见。(01:08:06)：非常感谢你的收听。如果你觉得有价值，可以在 Apple Podcasts、Spotify 或你喜欢的播客 app 上订阅。也请考虑给我们评分或留评，这真的能帮到其他听众发现这档播客。你可以在 lennyspodcast.com 找到所有往期节目或了解更多。下期见。
